idle.robotsCheckTitle: Checks the page's robots.txt to see whether this URL is allowed for crawlers
idle.combinedHint: Merges several of your own already-saved configurations — even from different sites — into one script whose outputs are combined into a single result.
idle.combinedNoSavedConfigsHint: No saved configurations yet — save at least two configurations first (in another mode), then combine them here.
idle.apiCaptureTitle: Records this page's fetch/XHR network requests
idle.apiSearchTitle: Then click a data point on the page — it will be searched for in the recording
idle.apiEmbeddedJsonSearchTitle: For sites with no separate network request: click a data point and it will be searched for in the page's own <script> tags (e.g. __NEXT_DATA__)
idle.apiEntriesTitle: Shows every network request recorded so far, with URL, method and status
idle.previewTitle: Shows directly on the page which elements the current configuration would match
idle.exportConfigTitle: Export the current fields/containers as JSON — e.g. for a bug report
idle.saveConfigTitle: Save the current configuration locally, so it can be reloaded next time this site is scraped
idle.savedConfigsEmpty: No saved configurations for this site yet.
idle.savedOutputsEmpty: No saved outputs for this configuration yet.
idle.hardeningReplayNoChecks: No hardening checks are currently configured — set one up in the Monitoring section first.
idle.hardeningReplayCompareBasisLabel: This check needs a previous result to compare against:
idle.engineBrowserTitle: Renders JavaScript before extraction — for dynamically loaded pages or login flows. Slower than the static engine.
idle.outputFileToggle: Download the full scraped data file
idle.additionalUrlsPlaceholder: One URL per line (in addition to the page above)
idle.changeDetectionHint: Every field here is the name of an environment variable, not the value itself — the real value is read from the environment at the actual run, never written into the script.
idle.proxyHint: The name of an environment variable holding a comma-separated list of proxy URLs (e.g. "http://user:pass@host:port"), not the addresses themselves — with more than one, the script rotates through them per request.
idle.requestDelayHint: The script waits between two requests to the site — fixed, or randomly within a range (e.g. 1 to 3). Protects against blocks and rate limits, but makes the run correspondingly longer (e.g. 50 pages × 2 s ≈ 1.5 minutes more). The trial run when generating doesn't count the pauses against its time limit.
idle.respectRobotsDelayHint: If the site's robots.txt asks for a pace (Crawl-delay or Request-rate), the script waits at least that long between two requests. Sites that publish nothing are unaffected. Combined with "Pause between requests", the larger gap wins. The robots.txt is read once per run.
idle.robotsDisallowToggle: Check the site's robots.txt before every request
idle.robotsDisallowHint: The script reads the site's robots.txt while it runs and checks each request (pages, further pages, downloads, API calls) against its Disallow rules — in case the site changed them after you created this script. An unreadable robots.txt never blocks anything; no robots.txt means no restrictions. The robots.txt is read once per run.
idle.appendOutputToggle: Append to the existing output file instead of replacing it
idle.appendOutputHint: Every run adds its result to the output file left by the previous runs (CSV rows, JSON entries, XML elements, SQLite rows, Excel rows), so the file grows into an archive. If the data's fields change between runs, the file's columns stay and new ones are added; missing values stay empty. If the existing file can't be read or has a different shape, the run stops without touching it. The first run (no file yet) simply creates it. Not for combined mode.
idle.retryExponentialToggle: Double the wait after every retry
idle.retryHint: If a request fails with a connection error, a timeout or one of the status codes, the script tries it again after the wait (for 429/503 as long as the server asks via Retry-After; at most 60 s per wait). Other errors such as 404 or 403 fail immediately. If every attempt fails, the run stops as before.
idle.dedupKeyFieldsHint: Pick the field(s) that identify an item (together they form its key). A later row/element with a key that already appeared in this run is dropped — useful for overlapping pages or items reachable from several start URLs. Items whose key fields are all empty are never removed.
idle.dedupIncrementalToggle: Only write new items since the last run
idle.dedupOutputDeltaTitle: The output file contains just the items that are new in this run (it is replaced on every run).
idle.dedupOutputAppendTitle: New items are appended to the output file of the previous runs, so it grows into a collection of everything seen.
idle.dedupIncrementalHint: The script remembers the keys it has seen in a small file next to its output (output file name + .dedup-seen.json). Delete that file to start over. The remembered keys are bounded: either by number (the newest ones are kept) or by age. The file is only updated after a run that did not fail a hardening check.
idle.requestHeaderTestValuePlaceholder: Test value for the trial run (not saved)
idle.requestHeadersHint: Sent with every request of the script — useful for a language (Accept-Language), a Referer, an API key or a Cookie. Put secrets in an environment variable and enter only its name here; the one-time test value is used for the trial run only and is never saved or written into the script. A header named User-Agent replaces the default one. With the browser engine, the headers go to every request the page makes.
idle.externalConfigHint: Lets you tweak the start URL(s), the output filename, a field's output name, or a fixed-value-list API parameter's values later, by editing a small XML file — without touching the .py file or reopening the extension. The file doesn't exist yet; the script creates it next to itself the first time it actually runs.
idle.paginationUrlTemplateHint: Must contain both {url} (the start page, unchanged) and {page} (the page number, starting at 2 — page 1 is always the start page as-is).
idle.discoveredUrlsHint: Loads this page once and adds every link matching the selector, in addition to the URL above and any additional start URLs. A link can also be picked by its text, e.g. a:contains("Vegetables").
idle.discoveredUrlsMaxUrlsLabel: Max. number of discovered URLs (safety limit)
idle.hardeningSeverityWarningTitle: The script prints a warning but still exits with code 0.
idle.hardeningSeverityErrorTitle: The script prints an error and exits with its own code (2), distinguishable from a crash (1).
idle.hardeningNullRateSectionLabel: Check for empty values per field
idle.hardeningBaselineToggle: Check for a drop vs. the last run
idle.hardeningBlockingToggle: Check for blocking (redirect, short response, block phrases)
idle.hardeningBlockingPhrasesPlaceholder: e.g. "Access Denied", "Please verify you are human"
idle.preflightToggle: Check beforehand whether the page has changed, and skip the run if not
idle.preflightHint: Sends a quick request to the page before the real scrape starts. If nothing has changed since the last run, or the page isn't reachable right now, the run is skipped without the cost of a full scrape.
idle.blocksHint: Builds several independent extraction blocks (flat or container, freely mixed) sharing this page’s navigation — each writes its own output file in one script run.
idle.blocksMinCountHint: At least 2 blocks are required to generate a script.
idle.outputBlueprintMappingHint: Map each target field to one of this configuration's own source fields — every target field needs a source before the script can be generated.
idle.outputBlueprintTreeMappingHint: Map each target field to one of this configuration's own source fields — a target group's own position in the output is inferred automatically from its mapped fields. Every target field needs a source before the script can be generated.
idle.outputFormatFlattenHint: Nested results are flattened into one table: one row per innermost repeating item, with values from higher levels repeated in every row (or pick an Output Blueprint to choose the columns yourself). Every data field needs a unique name.

apiConfig.embeddedJsonSourceNote: Sourced from embedded JSON in the page's own <script> tag ({selector}) — the URL below is the page to fetch, not a JSON API endpoint.
apiConfig.insertParameterHint: Inserts the placeholder at the end (or at the cursor position if you just clicked into the field) — move it yourself to the right spot in the path afterward, where a fixed value would otherwise go, e.g. ".../categories/{category}/weeks".
apiConfig.valueListPlaceholder: Values, comma-separated or one per line
apiConfig.autoFillFromPoolTitle: Searches the recorded request pool for other calls with the same URL shape and adds their differing values to the list
apiConfig.autoFillNoMatches: No further values found in the recording.
apiConfig.bodyCoerceToTitle: Value type to use in the body (default: text)

apiCursor.hint: For APIs that only reveal the next page's cursor inside the current response (e.g. pageInfo.endCursor or next_page_token). The script fetches page after page for every parameter combination until no cursor is returned.
apiCursor.detectNone: Nothing cursor-like found in the recorded request/response. Enter the paths manually.
apiCursor.detectApplied: Cursor settings filled in from the recording — please check them.
apiCursor.nextCursorPathLabel: Next cursor in the response (JSON path)
apiCursor.bodyNeedsPost: A body target needs a POST request with a recorded request body.
apiCursor.firstPageHint: Page 1 is sent exactly as recorded — make sure the recorded request is the first page, without a cursor.

apiLink.hint: For APIs (GitHub, GitLab, WordPress, ...) that announce the next page in the HTTP Link response header instead of in the body. The script requests that URL page after page for every parameter combination until no next link is left. Not for POST requests.
apiLink.detectedHint: A recorded response announced a next page via a Link header — this option probably fits.
apiLink.needsGet: Link-header pagination needs a GET request.
apiLink.firstPageHint: Page 1 is sent exactly as recorded — make sure the recorded request is the first page. Next-page links to another host are never followed.

apiBootstrap.toggleLabel: Fetch a fresh token before every run (auth bootstrap)
apiBootstrap.hint: For APIs that need a short-lived token from a login/token request first. The script sends that request at the start of every run and uses the extracted value in the headers/URL below — credentials only ever come from environment variables.
apiBootstrap.recordingHint: Pick the login/token request. Not listed? Keep recording, reload the page (or log in again), then reopen this list.
apiBootstrap.recordingEmpty: No recorded request with a JSON response found.
apiBootstrap.recordingLikely: token used by the main request
apiBootstrap.recordingApplied: Token request adopted — value read from "{path}".
apiBootstrap.recordingNoValuePath: Token request adopted, but the token's JSON path couldn't be detected — please enter it.
apiBootstrap.bodyFieldsLabel: Body fields of the token request
apiBootstrap.valuePathLabel: JSON path to the token in the response
apiBootstrap.usageHint: Use {placeholder} in a header ("From token" mode, e.g. Bearer {placeholder}) or pick "Token value" as the value source of a URL part. Discovery requests reuse the headers.
apiBootstrap.sourceKindNote: Filled with the freshly fetched token ({placeholder}) on every run.
apiBootstrap.sourceKindMissing: No auth bootstrap configured — enable it above or pick another value source.

transformPresets.saveUnavailableHint: The companion isn't reachable or is too old — your own presets aren't available right now.
transformPresets.settingsHint: Save a transformation chain from a field's dialog with "Save as preset", then apply it to any field via "Apply preset …".
transformPresets.unavailableHint: Your own presets aren't available (companion unreachable or too old) — only the built-in ones are shown.

settings.title: Settings
settings.scriptNameHostnameHint: The script name is always derived from the current website's hostname.
settings.outputFormatHint: The file the generated script writes. SQLite and Excel contain one table / sheet; nested results (containers, nested API data) are flattened into it. Excel needs the Python package "openpyxl" (pip install openpyxl) on the machine running the script and the companion. Not available for blocks or combined mode; cannot be combined with change detection.
settings.skipVerificationToggle: Skip the trial run (return the script immediately)
settings.skipVerificationHint: The companion normally runs the generated script once against the live page before handing it out, which proves it works but takes time. With this on, the script is returned right away without being run — it is still checked for structural problems (broken URL, duplicate or empty field names), but a wrong selector or a blocked request only shows up when you run it yourself. A data preview or a full output file isn't available while this is on.
settings.accessKeyHint: Only needed when the companion you connect to requires a personal access key (several people sharing one companion). Whoever runs the companion creates it for you. It is stored in this browser and sent with every request to the companion.
settings.accessKeyNotNeeded: This companion does not use access keys.
settings.accessKeyMissing: This companion requires an access key.
settings.accessKeyRejected: The access key is not valid.
settings.accessKeyUnreachable: The companion could not be reached.

account.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices have to sign in again.
account.noRegistration: This companion does not allow self-registration — ask whoever runs it for an account or an access key.

account.passwordMismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
account.unreachable: The companion could not be reached.
account.throttled: Too many attempts — try again in {seconds} seconds.
account.failed: The companion answered with an error (HTTP {status}).

browserActions.title: Browser actions
browserActions.hint: Run in order before extraction, e.g. for a login flow.
browserActions.envVarHint: The value is read from this environment variable at runtime, never stored in the script.
browserActions.testValueHint: Used only for the one-time trial run when generating — never stored, never included in the script.
browserActions.persistentSessionHint: Saves cookies/login state after each run and skips the login actions above on the next run. Warning: the saved file contains live session cookies — treat it like a password and never share or commit it. If the session ever expires, the run simply fails; there is no automatic re-login.
